text: card_reply's length is task-specific, not universal. The read-peers phase asks for 'one or two plain sentences per peer'; no other phase specifies a range.
No rule in the codebase says card_reply 'must always be two or three plain sentences' as a universal constraint.

A task mastermind may NOT spawn a second task mastermind yet, but this is conditional: 'depth stops at two UNTIL one measured run proves a three-deep tree can report failure upward' (sub-mastermind SKILL.md line 89).
The no-nesting-yet rule is experimental, not foundational—it exists because the claim has never been tested, not because nesting always breaks.
Server/merge.mjs is 'the one serialized way to land a worktree' (its header line 1–2), preventing two merges from running at once via a lock file.
Server/merge.mjs itself runs 'git merge --no-ff' for clean merges with no overlapping uncommitted work in the main tree (line 350).
The review gate in merge.mjs (line 85+) is a GATE, not a mandate to use merge.mjs for all merges—it only refuses branches sized 'light' or 'full' that lack a review.
A merge of size 'none' (only CSS or docs, 20 lines or fewer, no new file—per review.md line 60–61) bypasses the review gate entirely and presumably could use plain git merge.
Card_reply's length bends in every phase after read-peers: brief/revise/vote/names/implement phases give no sentence limit, only content direction.
The no-second-mastermind rule bends when a measured run proves a three-level tree can report failure upward—this is explicitly the intended exit ramp.
The merge-via-merge.mjs rule bends for size 'none' (review gate skipped), and merge.mjs itself delegates to 'git merge --no-ff' when there's no conflict.
